slides.title:
*Cyber Monday*
was invented by
a press release.

Shop.org, part of the
*National Retail Federation*,
spots a spike.
slides.sub:
Online sales jump the Monday after
Thanksgiving: people are back at work,
with faster internet than at home.

slides.title:
Google results for
*"Cyber Monday"* in 2005.

names they dropped:
*Black Monday*, Blue Monday,
Green Monday.
slides.sub:
"Black Monday"? Already taken by the
greatest stock market crash of all time,
says Davis (Fast Company).

slides.title:
The Wall Street Journal
picks up the release.
*Then everyone does.*
slides.sub:
"We had no idea that 'Cyber Monday' would
be picked up by the media as much
as it was." (Scott Silverman, eMarketer)

slides.title:
It wasn't even the biggest
online day back then.
*It became one.*
slides.sub:
"It was definitely a self-fulfilling
prophecy" (Silverman). $608M in 2006,
over $1B in one day by 2010 (comScore).

slides.title:
spent online in the US on
Cyber Monday 2025. *+7.1%.*
slides.sub:
57.5% on mobile. $1.03B paid with
Buy Now, Pay Later (Adobe, Dec. 2, 2025).

slides.title: We spoke the word into existence and *we really haven't been able to escape it since.*
slides.author:
Ellen Davis
then at the National Retail Federation
(Fast Company, 2015)

slides.title:
A name + a date
= *a moment.*
slides.sub:
A press release turned a random Monday
into a $14B day. Black Friday is tomorrow.
Cyber Monday is Nov. 30.

✅ Name your offer (not just "-20%")
